neet_phy_u03_t05_1.working: Maximum static friction is 0.4 × 50 = 20 N. The 10 N push is below this, so the box stays at rest and static friction equals the push, 10 N.

neet_phy_u03_t05_3.working: The force is minimum when pulled at tanθ = μ, giving Fmin = μmg/√(1+μ²) = 0.75 × 40 / 1.25 = 24 N.

neet_phy_u03_t05_4.working: Angle of friction = tan⁻¹μs, which equals the angle of repose (II). Static friction matches the applied force up to μsN (IV). Kinetic friction = μkN (I). Rolling friction is much smaller than sliding friction (III).

neet_phy_u03_t05_5.working: A is true. B is true, because pulling upward reduces N while pushing downward increases it. C is false, since friction on the foot acts forward. D is false, since μk < μs. E is true. So A, B and E.
